newsitem.title: FRANCE: French voters oppose Thomson sell-off.
newsitem.headline: French voters oppose Thomson sell-off.

text.p: French voters overwhelmingly oppose government plans to sell the heavily-indebted Thomson SA state group to the private sector for a symbolic one franc, according to an opinion poll released on Sunday.

The survey of 1,004 voters to be published on Monday by the business daily La Tribune Desfosses said 72 percent disapproved of the sale for the symbolic price to the Lagardere conglomerate because it did not reflect the group's value.
Twelve percent said the sale was right because of the group's heavy debts.

The conservative French government wants to privatise and sell Thomson, allowing Lagardere to retain the CSF defence arm and dispose of its consumer electronics group Thomson Multimedia to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics also for one franc.
Forty-five percent of those questioned said they opposed the privatisation to 34 percent who supported it.

Sixty-six percent said the state should not relinquish ownership of an ailing public company, even if it meant propping it up with taxpapyers money. Twenty-two percent said they preferred it to be privatised even if it should be sold to a foreign company.
The opposition Socialists and Communists in France's National Assembly have called for a committee of inquiry into the conditions of Thomson's privatisation.
